perplexity.description:
Spawn: The Album is a 1997 soundtrack released by Immortal Records to accompany the live-action film adaptation of the comic book character. As a compilation featuring various artists working across electronic, rock, and cinematic styles, the album reflects the eclectic sonic palette typical of mid-1990s film soundtracks that sought to bridge mainstream rock and alternative music audiences. The project showcased Immortal Records' expanding reach beyond traditional band signings into soundtrack production, positioning the label as a tastemaker in both music and visual media.

The album achieved notable commercial success, reaching number 7 on the Billboard 200 and earning RIAA Gold certification in the United States. This performance demonstrated the soundtrack's appeal beyond dedicated film fans, resonating with rock and electronic music listeners of the era. The compilation's success contributed to Immortal Records' profile during a period when the label was establishing itself as a significant independent force in alternative and rock music.

The Spawn soundtrack represents a snapshot of mid-1990s popular music, capturing the era's embrace of genre-blending and multimedia tie-ins. Its commercial achievement underscored the viability of soundtrack albums as standalone musical products during this period, when film soundtracks could achieve platinum status and chart prominence comparable to traditional studio albums.
